title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 98-100): Grothendieck is making 'Legendre pinnings' (épinglages de Legendre) of an elliptic curve in characteristic ≠ 2 explicit in coordinates.

The data are (J, F_t ⊂ V_J(k), t, ν).
- J is a finite set; most likely the 3-element set of nonzero 2-torsion points (equivalently the finite Weierstrass roots e_i).
- V_J = Ker(k^J → k, sum).
- t is the tangent line at the origin.
- F_t is a line in V_J.
- ν is an isomorphism t^{⊗2} ≅ F_t^{⊗2}(ω).
- ω = ω_J is a 2-element set, identified by α with μ_4^*, the primitive 4th roots of unity.

The Lemma on p. 98 identifies a pinning with a pair (α, (ψ^ω(δ))), where ψ^ω(δ) ∈ F_t is indexed by ω ∈ ω and δ ∈ t^* (nonzero cotangent vectors, i.e. invariant differentials). The family must satisfy (71) and (72), which relate the two ω's and give homogeneity in δ, and the quadratic condition (73): ψ^ω(δ)^{⊗2} = ν(δ^{⊗2}) ∧ ω.

This page writes the family in coordinates as a 3-index family ψ_i^ω(δ) ∈ k, with i ∈ J:
- (75) Σ_i ψ_i^ω(δ) = 0. This says ψ^ω(δ) lies in V_J.
- (76) ψ_i^{ω'}(δ) = i_ω ψ_i^ω(δ). Switching to the other element ω' multiplies by the 4th root of unity attached to ω via α.
- (77) ψ_i^ω(λδ) = λ^{-1} ψ_i^ω(δ). This is homogeneity of degree −1 in δ, i.e. modular 'weight 1'.

Next, F_t is presented as the plane cut out in k^J by Σλ_i = 0 together with a further linear form Σ c_i λ_i = 0. Here (e_i) is the canonical basis of k^J. The vector (c_i) is determined only modulo k^* and modulo adding a diagonal vector. Adding a diagonal vector is harmless because Σλ_i = 0. So (c_i) is a point of P(k^J / diagonal), which for |J| = 3 is essentially the λ-line coordinate.

Membership ψ^ω(δ) ∈ F_t becomes (78): Σ_i c_i ψ_i^ω(δ) = 0. Because F_t is a subspace and (76), (77) only rescale, it suffices to impose this for one pair (ω, δ).

What remains is to write (73) in coordinates. The next page starts a new section, 'IV Descriptions explicites par fonctions ℘ de Weierstrass'.

Interpretation: if c_i = e_i (Weierstrass roots), then F_t is spanned by (e_2−e_3, e_3−e_1, e_1−e_2). The ψ_i are weight-1 quantities whose squares relate to the differences e_j − e_k. Classically these are the θ-constant squares at level 4, but this is not stated on the page.

The page as a whole is a routine coordinate translation of the lemma on p. 98.
errors: No mathematical errors visible. The reduction 'it suffices to impose F_t-membership for one couple (ω,δ)' is correct, since (76),(77) are scalar rescalings and F_t is a linear subspace.
The meaning of i_ω in (76) is not defined on this page; presumably it is α^{-1}(ω) ∈ μ_4^*, or similar. The transcription marks it uncertain.
The displayed definition 'F_t = Σ_t{...}' is notationally odd. Since the c_i condition defines a subspace of V_J, it is presumably 'F_t = déf {...}' or similar.

ideas.what: Coordinate description of a Legendre-type level structure: a family ψ_i^ω(δ) ∈ k with Σ_i ψ_i = 0, a μ_4-twist relation, weight −1 homogeneity in the differential, and linear constraint Σ c_i ψ_i = 0
ideas.modern_name: Level-(2,4) / Legendre-form structure on elliptic curves; weight-1 modular forms of level 4 (theta-constant squares) as coordinates
ideas.usually_credited_to: Legendre and Jacobi classically; Igusa and Deligne–Rapoport for moduli; Katz for modular forms as functions of (E, ω)

ideas.what: Parametrizing the 2-dimensional subspace F_t ⊂ k^J by a vector (c_i) defined modulo scalars and diagonal (affine invariance of Weierstrass roots)
ideas.modern_name: Weierstrass roots up to affine change; λ-invariant as a point of P(k^J/k)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a mechanical translation of a lemma into explicit coordinate equations. It contains no new construction or result. The surrounding Legendre-pinning framework (a μ_4-indexed weight-1 'Katz-style' description) is somewhat interesting, but this page adds only bookkeeping.
transcription_corrections: 'F_t = \sum_t {...}' probably reads 'F_t = déf {...}' or similar; a defining symbol, not a sum.
The '(77)' with Σ ψ_i^ω(δ) e_i near the middle is crossed out in the manuscript. It is distinct from the genuine (77) homogeneity relation.
'\underline{\Sigma}\, k^J' in the NB is likely just 'de k^J' with an underlined/decorated symbol; reading uncertain.
't^*_{[?]}' in line 'définis par les (ω,δ) ∈ ω × t^*' has a small subscript, possibly a struck letter; immaterial.
The marginal note reads '(e_i)_{i∈J} base canonique de k^J'.
